# Schema objects Rust creates that Go's migrations do not: the ONLY differences the schema
# fingerprint test (crates/fc-platform/tests/it/schema_fingerprint_test.rs) allows.
# One line prefix per entry, matched against the fingerprint line. Every entry must match at
# least one line (a stale entry fails the test), and Go has no object that Rust lacks.
# All are additive and nullable/unused by Go: Go reads with explicit column lists.

# Rust's own function registry (migration 062). Parity plan D1: fng_* is the schema of record
# (migration 079); fnr_* stays until the function code moves to fng_* in P4, then is dropped.
table fnr_
column fnr_
index fnr_
constraint fnr_

# Rust 058
column app_client_configs.base_url_override 
column app_client_configs.config_json 
# Rust 059
column iam_principal_roles.assigned_by 
# Rust 060
column iam_service_accounts.wh_header_name 
column iam_service_accounts.wh_password_ref 
column iam_service_accounts.wh_signature_header 
column iam_service_accounts.wh_username 
# Rust 061
column msg_dispatch_jobs_read.queue
